title: Corpus Hermeticum I (Poemandres), X (The Key), XIII (Secret Sermon on the Mountain), in Thrice-Greatest Hermes vol. II
author: Hermetic authors; trans. G. R. S. Mead
edition_cited: Theosophical Publishing Society, London 1906, vol. II
summary: Three Hermetic treatises with light-vision under sense-withdrawal. CH I: while meditating, with bodily senses held back as in heavy sleep, Hermes sees 'a Vision limitless, all things turned into Light'; at the end 'closing of the eyes' is 'true vision'. CH X: the vision of the Good does not dazzle like sunlight but increases the eye's seeing, a radiance 'the mind alone can see'; the gazer stills every sense and motion, and it shines round his mind and draws the soul out of the body. CH XIII: 'Withdraw into thyself... throw out of work the body's senses' and rebirth comes; the reborn knows himself made of Light and Life.
why_relevant: The western root text for sense-withdrawal leading to a vision of light; tests whether a practice is stated.
